finding.claim: Unauthenticated SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL query, allowing arbitrary read of the SQLite database via UNION SELECT.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: /search route is registered with no auth guard
q read from request args with no validation or escaping
value interpolated directly into SQL text via f-string
result rows returned as JSON to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, allowlist, or auth guard on the route. No framework middleware in app.py sanitizes input. sqlite3 execute runs a single statement, so stacked writes are not possible, but UNION SELECT reads are. Parameterized queries are used on /product and /by-owner, not on /search.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /search route (app.py:9-10) has no auth decorator or before_request hook, and app.py:11 reads q raw. app.py:12 interpolates it into an f-string SQL query with no escaping or allowlist. app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON. Parameterized queries exist only on /product (app.py:18) and /by-owner (app.py:25), not on /search.
verdict.reason: Anonymous users can reach /search (app.py:9-10), and the raw q value is concatenated into the SQL string at app.py:12, so a quote-breaking payload such as `' UNION SELECT ... --` can read other tables and the rows are returned to the caller at app.py:13. Nothing in app.py validates, escapes, or parameterizes that value.
